## Novelty pre-check

Verdict: **trivial_or_ill_posed**. A short argument proves this. Write n = t*s^2 with t squarefree, so A000188(n) = s. n*k is a square iff t*k is a square iff k = t*m^2 (since t is squarefree). The bound k <= n gives m <= s, so the right-hand side counts exactly s values of k. The left-hand side (solutions of x^2 == 0 mod n) also equals s, which is the defining characterization (1) of A000188 and easy to check prime by prime. The identity therefore holds for every n >= 1. The 'Yanev's conjecture is true (see Fried link)' part reads as an already-settled claim. None of the search results is relevant, so no R-ref is cited; the verdict rests on the argument alone.
